subsystems.name: Inner ring
subsystems.role: a continuous loop or stream of pellets moving faster than orbital velocity, providing outward force.

subsystems.name: Outer ring
subsystems.role: a stationary shell encircling the planet, held up by magnetic repulsion from the inner ring.

subsystems.name: Magnetic coupling
subsystems.role: transfers force between the moving inner ring and the stationary outer ring.

subsystems.name: Power and propulsion
subsystems.role: accelerates the inner ring and replaces energy lost to friction and drag.

subsystems.name: Access and launch systems
subsystems.role: moves people and cargo between the surface and the ring.

subsystems.name: Station-keeping and stabilization
subsystems.role: keeps the ring aligned and counteracts perturbations from the Moon, Sun and atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Develop ultra-strong materials
buildSteps.detail: manufacture kilometre-scale fibres or films with strength-to-weight ratios far beyond steel or carbon fibre, such as carbon nanotubes or diamond nanothreads.

buildSteps.title: Establish orbital assembly
buildSteps.detail: use current and future launch systems to place construction robots and materials in low Earth orbit.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the inner ring
buildSteps.detail: assemble a continuous loop or pellet stream and accelerate it electromagnetically to above orbital velocity.

buildSteps.title: Build the outer ring
buildSteps.detail: construct a stationary segmented shell around the inner ring, using magnetic levitation to hold it aloft.

buildSteps.title: Install power and control
buildSteps.detail: add linear accelerators, power supplies and control systems to maintain the inner ring's speed and stability.

buildSteps.title: Add access infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: attach space elevators or launch loops to move payloads from the surface to the ring.

buildSteps.title: Expand for habitation and industry
buildSteps.detail: build habitats, factories and solar power arrays on the outer ring.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: run the ring as a launch loop and spaceport, with continuous maintenance to replace worn parts.

prerequisites.why: no known material can yet be made in the required lengths and quantities to withstand the forces.
demonstrated in trains and labs, but not at the scale or reliability needed for a planetary ring.
the International Space Station shows assembly is possible, but not at megastructure scale.
reusable rockets have cut costs, but thousands of tonnes would still be needed.
software and thrusters exist, but a ring's dynamics are far more complex.

pathway.unlocks: experience with long, moving structures in orbit.

pathway.milestone: sub-scale orbital ring prototype in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: proof of magnetic support and energy transfer.

pathway.milestone: habitation and industry on the ring
